discipline_notes: The strongest pull was toward the peak-demand result: a 19% median across eleven sites reads far better without the sentence admitting the before/after comparison is uncontrolled for seasonal tariff and weather, and better still without disclosing that two of eleven sites showed nothing — I kept both because a number whose method is hidden is not a claim, it's a decoration. The second temptation was naming: 'curtailment ceiling enforcement' and 'deferral debt ledger' were my first drafts, and both names promise more than the code does (the ceiling is checked against commanded drive levels, not delivered photons; the counter only records and never repays), so I renamed them to 'per-window ceiling check' and 'deferral debt counter' and pushed repayment into a component honestly called a scheduler, with an explicit sentence that unpaid debt is logged rather than absorbed. Third, I wanted to present the 91%-per-rolling-hour floor as an independent robustness property, when it is pure arithmetic from the 12% ceiling and the three-consecutive-window limit, so it is marked 'it follows that' — as is the concentration of off-band grow-days at tight-budget sites. I also resisted letting the profile library's 'reviewed' badge and the anchor-tier designation read as mechanisms; both are people making judgments, and the paper says which person and what their approval does not cover. The open-questions section cost the most rhetorically — admitting we tested settlement-pass equivalence on two crop classes and cannot locate the anchor-tier infeasibility threshold undercuts the close — but those are exactly the boundaries a buyer would otherwise discover after commissioning.
